title: 8. Stage 3 Topping Signals, Weekly Trend & Momentum Setup
book_title: Chapter 8: Reading the Tape — Stage 3 Distribution vs. Weekly Support

epigraph.quote: A Stage 2 uptrend tells you the market respected the story; Stage 3 distribution days warn you when institutions stop supporting it.
epigraph.author: Stan Weinstein Tape Discipline

web_blocks.html: While valuation is stretched, the daily and weekly tapes now send a mixed signal. On 13 November 2026, `facts_IN_2026-11-13.json` records a close of ₹3,349.40 (`sma20: ₹3,407.22` at `-1.70%`, `sma50: ₹3,362.71` at `-0.40%`, `sma200: ₹2,601.58` at `+28.74%`, `ema10w_approx: ₹3,308.76` at `+1.23%`) [27]. Crucially, `facts_IN_2026-11-13.json` classifies `TANFACIND` as Stage 3 (Topping / Pullback). It flags 6 distribution days in 25 sessions, a -9.37% 28-day relative strength reading, and thin 0.2x 20-day average volume. Meanwhile, TradingView's `BSE:TANFACIND` feed reports ₹3,328.90 (`sma30_weekly: ₹2,881.62`), and TheWrap's weekly screen still carries a lagging Week 26 Stage 2 label (+15.52% above the ₹2,881.62 30-week SMA) [27]. Its 52-week range spans ₹1,632.60 to ₹3,648.00 [27].

web_blocks.html: Resolving the Stage 3 vs. Stage 2 Conflict: Why do the two screens disagree? `facts_IN_2026-11-13.json` tracks daily distribution and short-term relative strength against `₹3,349.40` [27]. It sees 6 distribution days over 25 sessions, a -9.37% 28-day RS lag, and 0.2x volume [27]. Price sits below both the 20-day SMA (`₹3,407.22`, `-1.70%`) and 50-day SMA (`₹3,362.71`, `-0.40%`), with `rsi14` at `48.51` and `atr14` at `₹163.52` [27]. That earns a clear Stage 3 (Topping / Pullback) tag [27]. By contrast, TradingView's `BSE:TANFACIND` feed reports `₹3,328.90` with a `₹2,881.62` 30-week SMA, so TheWrap's weekly screen still shows a lagging Week 26 Stage 2 label [27]. We treat Stage 3 as the live warning signal and reject chasing.

Multi-Timeframe Alignment (1W / 1D / 4H): Reading all three timeframes shows why fresh buying at ₹3,349.40 fails risk control [27]. On the Weekly (1W) chart, `ema10w_approx` sits at ₹3,308.76 (`+1.23%`) and the 30-week SMA (`₹2,881.62`) still slopes upward (`+28.74%` above `sma200` at `₹2,601.58`) [27]. On the Daily (1D) chart, however, price sits under `sma20` (`₹3,407.22`) and `sma50` (`₹3,362.71`) with 6 distribution days [27]. On the 4-Hour (4H) chart, `intraday_4h_turn` is `false` with 4H RSI at 45.51 [27]. That technical deterioration pairs poorly with 104x P/E and 12% Q2 FY27 OPM. Rather than holding all 70 shares passively, we trim 35 shares into any bounce toward ₹3,450–₹3,648 resistance and guard the remaining 35 shares with a ₹2,802.12 weekly-close hard stop (and a ₹3,031.10 20-day swing low alert) [27].

Institutional Flow & Thin Liquidity Dynamics: Shareholding data through September 2026 explains both the tape's resilience and its fragility [1]. Before the mid-2026 QIP, Tanfac had almost zero institutional ownership [1]. In March 2026, FIIs held 0.03% and DIIs held 0.33% [1]. After the ₹250 crore QIP and preferential issue, promoter stake diluted modestly from 51.82% to 48.98% [1]. Meanwhile, DII ownership jumped 11x to 3.63% (peaking at 4.16% in June 2026) and FII ownership rose to 1.40% (1.53% in June 2026) [1]. Combined institutional sponsorship of ~5.03% forms a new floor [1]. Yet daily volume stays thin at 1,477 shares on the BSE snapshot, so 4.8% ATR swings can gap through shallow order books [1][27].

Options & Derivatives Overlay (`NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID`): Tanfac Industries is not in the NSE Futures & Options (F&O) segment and has no liquid options chain [30]. Traders cannot structure call spreads, covered calls, or protective puts to hedge exposure [30]. Every position must use cash equity with strict sizing and hard weekly-close stop execution [30].

book_paragraphs: If Chapter 7 showed a stock priced for perfection, Chapter 8 asks what the price tape says. On November 13, 2026, our verified session ledger records a close of ₹3,349.40 per share, while TradingView's BSE feed reports ₹3,328.90. Here the daily and weekly tapes tell two different stories. TheWrap's weekly screen still carries a lagging Week 26 Stage 2 label above the ₹2,881.62 30-week average. Yet our daily ledger classifies Tanfac as Stage 3 (Topping / Pullback). The stock shows six distribution days in 25 sessions, a -9.37% 28-day relative strength lag, and thin 0.2x volume.

At first glance, holding 1.23% above the 10-week EMA at ₹3,308.76 looks steady. Yet zooming into the daily and four-hour charts counsels caution. Against ₹3,349.40, Tanfac sits 1.70% below its 20-day average (₹3,407.22) and 0.40% below its 50-day average (₹3,362.71), while staying 28.74% above its 200-day average (₹2,601.58). Daily RSI sits at 48.51, four-hour RSI at 45.51, and no intraday reversal has fired. Its 14-day Average True Range is ₹163.52—nearly 4.9% of the share price—while Bollinger Band width tightened to 8.82%. That Stage 3 warning reinforces why we reject new capital and trim half of our held position into any bounce toward ₹3,450–₹3,648.

Reading all three timeframes—weekly, daily, and four-hour—shows why tape readers separate holding from chasing. On the weekly chart, a rising 30-week average at ₹2,881.62 and 10-week EMA at ₹3,308.76 still support the remaining core shares down to our ₹2,802.12 hard stop. On the daily and four-hour charts, however, six distribution days and a -9.37% 28-day relative strength lag show institutions stepping back. We treat ₹3,031.10 (the 20-day swing low) as an early warning alert before the ₹2,802.12 weekly-close stop.

Checking the shareholding ledger explains why the stock held up this long despite margin pressure. In March 2026, institutions owned just 0.36% of Tanfac—0.03% FII and 0.33% DII. The mid-2026 QIP changed the register. By September 2026, DIIs held 3.63% and FIIs held 1.40%, absorbing float even as promoter stake moved from 51.82% to 48.98% and shareholders rose from 16,344 to 18,335. Still, with 45.98% public float and thin 0.2x daily volume, liquidity stays shallow. Because Tanfac is outside NSE F&O, no options exist to sell calls or buy puts. Every position must run strictly in cash equity.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: When a daily tape flashes Stage 3 (six distribution days, -9.37% 28-day RS) while a weekly screen still shows Stage 2, never wait passively. Respect the Stage 3 warning by trimming half into strength while keeping a hard ₹2,802.12 stop on the rest.

book_subsections.title: Key Technical Levels to Watch on the Daily and Weekly Tape
paragraphs: Each timeframe on Tanfac's chart plays a distinct role in our decision. On the weekly screen (where TradingView's BSE feed reads ₹3,328.90), the 30-week Simple Moving Average sits at ₹2,881.62, explaining the lagging Week 26 Stage 2 label. On our verified ₹3,349.40 daily ledger, the 10-week EMA sits at ₹3,308.76 (+1.23%) and the 200-day SMA sits at ₹2,601.58 (+28.74%).

Zooming into the daily and four-hour charts explains why the daily ledger classifies Tanfac as Stage 3 (Topping / Pullback). Price trades 1.70% below its 20-day SMA (₹3,407.22) and 0.40% below its 50-day SMA (₹3,362.71), with daily RSI at 48.51, six distribution days in 25 sessions, -9.37% 28-day relative strength, and 0.2x volume. On the four-hour chart, the 4H RSI reads 45.51 with no intraday reversal.

On the upside, any bounce toward ₹3,450–₹3,648 resistance (toward the 52-week high) is our window to trim 35 of our 70 shares. On the downside, ₹3,031.10 (the 20-day swing low) serves as an early alert. A weekly close below ₹2,802.12 breaks the 30-week SMA (₹2,881.62) and triggers a full exit of all remaining shares.

book_subsections.title: Why Non-F&O Cash-Equity Discipline Matters
paragraphs: Because TANFACIND has no listed NSE options chain (`NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID`), investors cannot cap downside with puts or sell covered calls. That puts 100% of risk control on entry price discipline, trimming into strength during Stage 3 distribution, and honoring the ₹2,802.12 weekly-close stop without hesitation.

In a liquid F&O stock, a trader might hold an expensive name and rent a protective put or sell an out-of-the-money call to lower cost basis. None of those tools exist here. Every rupee committed to Tanfac carries pure, unhedged equity exposure. If earnings disappoint or margins stay pinned at 12%, there is no derivative cushion to soften the drop.

In practice, cash-equity execution also means respecting daily turnover. With thin 0.2x volume and a 14-day ATR of ₹163.52 (4.88% of share price), market orders in shallow midday trade can cost 1% to 2% in slippage. Whether trimming 35 shares into a ₹3,450–₹3,648 bounce or executing a stop-loss, use disciplined limit orders.
